content.text:
The three bands fix Dq, B and C uniquely: **Dq ≈ 922 cm⁻¹, B ≈ 828 cm⁻¹, C ≈ 4260 cm⁻¹**, so C/B ≈ 5.2. The Co²⁺ free-ion values are about B ≈ 1115 cm⁻¹ and C/B ≈ 4.4, so B is reduced to roughly 0.74 of the free-ion value.

**Method.** I did not use the simplified Tanabe–Sugano formulas. I built the full d⁷ Hamiltonian in the basis of Slater determinants with M_s = ½, which is 120 determinants. It contains the Coulomb repulsion, parametrised by B and C (F₂ = B + 5F₄, F₄ = C/35), and an octahedral field of Dq. I then diagonalised it.

I identified the terms by two properties of the eigenvectors:
- Spin, from ⟨S²⟩.
- Orbital symmetry, from the C₄ character: T₁ gives +1, T₂ gives −1 and E gives 0.

The ⁴T₂, ⁴T₁(2) and ²T₁(2) levels, measured from the ⁴T₁ ground term, were then fitted to 8100, 19400 and 21600 cm⁻¹ by solving the three equations for Dq, B and C. The residuals are zero.

**Why the parameters are determined.** The quartet energies depend only on Dq and B, so ⁴T₂ and ⁴T₁(2) fix those two. The doublet ²T₁(2) is the only band that depends on C, so it fixes C.

**Predicted levels with these parameters** (cm⁻¹, measured from the ground term):

| Term | Energy |
|---|---|
| ⁴T₂ | 8100 (fitted) |
| ⁴A₂ | ≈17 300 (not observed; the ²T₁(1) doublet predicted at ≈17 100 lies in the same region) |
| ⁴T₁(2) | 19 400 (fitted) |
| ²T₁(2) | 21 600 (fitted) |

**Caveat.** C comes from a single spin-forbidden band, so it is much less certain than Dq and B. The C/B ≈ 5.2 is high.
